observations.explanation: The paper describes the hierarchical localization, context windows, search/replace patch format, filtering, and voting in useful detail (PDF pp. 4–6). But the claim that the design is fully “implementable” is stronger than the supplied text establishes: it gives some settings, yet not every prompt or implementation detail needed to reproduce the pipeline exactly.

The ablation reports 70 fixes for a single sample, 78 with multiple samples and majority voting, and 82 for the full system with test filtering (PDF p. 8). Thus filtering adds four fixes beyond voting in the reported setup.

The paper says baseline results are taken from the official leaderboard or each tool’s paper/repository, and notes that many leading baselines are closed-source (PDF pp. 6–7). This supports the stated limitation about controlled reruns and source availability.

The authors report that closed-source agent tools perform better than AGENTLESS when no location clue is provided, and identify this as future work (PDF p. 11). The observation accurately presents this as an acknowledged difficulty, not a demonstrated general failure beyond that category.
